title: Static files
summary: Serve HTML, CSS and other ready-made files from a folder with express.static.

options: A file the server sends exactly as it is stored, such as an image or CSS file
A file that never changes name
A file created by a route handler for each request
A file that only the server can read
quiz.explain: Static files need no code to produce them. Express just finds the file on disk and sends it.

quiz.q: Complete the line so files in the folder named public are served.
quiz.explain: `express.static(folderName)` creates the middleware, and `app.use` plugs it in.

quiz.q: The folder `public` contains `css/site.css`. The line is `app.use(express.static('public'))`. Which URL returns that file?
quiz.explain: The folder name is not part of the URL. Everything inside `public` is served from the root `/`.
The first argument of `app.use` is a prefix placed in front of the file paths.

quiz.q: A browser asks for the folder URL `/` and `public/index.html` exists. What happens with `express.static`?
options: A list of files is shown
quiz.explain: `express.static` sends `index.html` for a folder request by default, which is how a home page is served.

exercise.task:
Two folders already exist next to your program: `public` (with `index.html` and `hello.txt`) and `docs` (with `guide.txt`).

In `app.js`:

- Serve the `public` folder at the root of the site, so `/hello.txt` works and `/` shows the home page.
- Serve the `docs` folder under the prefix `/guide`, so `/guide/guide.txt` works.
- Keep the existing `GET /api/hi` route.

Use the folder names `'public'` and `'docs'` exactly as written. Leave `module.exports = app;` at the bottom.
hints: `express.static('public')` creates middleware for a folder. Plug it in with `app.use(...)`.
Without a prefix the folder is served at `/`. To put a folder under a prefix, give `app.use` the prefix first: `app.use('/guide', express.static('docs'))`.
